pr_body:
While we built the first version of `HealthMetadata` object, we use the `Settings` object, which has the Node's settings. Due to this we always used the default values of the settings. This makes that every time a new master was selected, the initial `HealthMetadata` was built with the default values instead of the settings configured by the user.

closes #96219

issue_context.title: max_shards_in_cluster is not properly calculated from max_shards_per_node
issue_context.body:
### Elasticsearch Version

8.6.0, 8.7.0, 8.8.0, 8.9.0

### Installed Plugins

ESS default

### Java Version

ESS default

### OS Version

ESS default

### Problem Description

Our clusters hit continuously the following error on ESS

It is related to the number of shards per cluster `max_shards_in_cluster` that is calculated based on `max_shards_per_node` but is not correctly calculated, our value for `max_shards_per_node` is 10000. We have 10 data nodes, so we have configured more than 7000 shards per cluster for sure. No matter the value you put on `max_shards_per_node`, we cannot have more than 7000 shards in our clusters.

![image](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/assets/5400788/b32b3025-6c49-4ea8-a793-3a3d8ff0d300)

```
      "shards_capacity" : {
        "status" : "Red",
        "symptom" : "Cluster is close to reaching the configured maximum number of shards for data nodes.",
        "details" : {
          "data" : {
            "max_shards_in_cluster" : 7000,
            "current_used_shards" : 9023
```

```
{
  "status": "green",
  "number_of_nodes": 10,
  "unassigned_shards": 0,
  "number_of_pending_tasks": 2,
  "number_of_in_flight_fetch": 0,
  "timed_out": false,
  "active_primary_shards": 5185,
  "task_max_waiting_in_queue_millis": 600,
  "cluster_name": "0000000000000000000000000",
  "relocating_shards": 0,
  "active_shards_percent_as_number": 100,
  "active_shards": 9753,
  "initializing_shards": 0,
  "number_of_data_nodes": 7,
  "delayed_unassigned_shards": 0
}
```

Probably related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/91119

### Steps to Reproduce

* Deploy a cluster with Elastic Stack 8.7.0
* Create more than 7000 shards
* Change the value of `max_shards_per_node` to 5000
* Wait until the error appears again

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_

>  `"number_of_data_nodes": 7,`

Apparently you have 7 data nodes, so 7000 is the right limit.
If I have `max_shards_per_node` to 5000 `max_shards_in_cluster` number should be `7*5000`, isn't it?
Sorry, I was confused by the "We have 10 data nodes" vs the `"number_of_data_nodes": 7,` bit. I see now. I think this is a health API problem.

Hi @kuisathaverat 

I've created a cluster to test this and it was impossible to replicate the issue. 
Looking at the shared settings and `_cluster/health` API response, I've some questions:

1. Do you have frozen nodes in this cluster? Frozen nodes are added up as part of the `_cluster/health API > number_of_data_nodes` total, but, for this indicator, they are not counted to calculate the number of total shards ([Documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/troubleshooting-shards-capacity-issues.html#_cluster_is_close_to_reaching_the_configured_maximum_number_of_shards_for_data_nodes)). 
Please share the response of `GET _nodes/stats/?filter_path=nodes.*.roles`. Anyway, looking at the value `max_shards_in_cluster = 7000` and `number_of_data_nodes = 7` makes me think that you don't have frozen nodes, and `max_shards_per_node` is configured to the default value of 1000.

2. Can you share the current `cluster.max_shard_per_node & cluster.max_shard_per_node.frozen`  values? `GET _cluster/settings?&include_defaults=true&filter_path=defaults.cluster.max_shards_per_node*`

3. > If I have `max_shards_per_node` to 5000 `max_shards_in_cluster` number should be 7*5000, isn't it?

Yes, it should be 7 * 5000, **only** if you have 7 nodes that **are not part** of the frozen tier

Looking forward to your comments

>are you saying that you previously changed the max_shards_per_node setting? wasn't it persisted in the cluster?

Yes, we increased it to `max_shards_per_node=2000` a few months ago, we did it several times until we realized that no matter the value of that parameter, we cannot have more `max_shards_in_cluster =date_nodes*1000`

>why do you say, "for a while"?

When we see the error in the cluster, we set a bigger `max_shards_per_node`. This makes the error disappear from the ESS UI for minutes/hours (I am not sure) but appears again if we are over the `max_shards_in_cluster =date_nodes*1000`. Last time before opening this issue we set `max_shards_per_node=15000` to be sure something weird happens, that value is not there anymore, I dunno what happens but for some reason, the value is set to 1000 again or never is set.

According to our private conversation, it's highly probable that the issue is within the setting value rather than the indicator itself. @kuisathaverat has fully restarted the cluster but the settings weren't restored to `1000`, so we have no idea what could be happening. Ivan will continue monitoring the cluster in case the setting is reverted.
marking as `>non-issue` but will keep it open for a couple of days just in case
So far no changes, if the next week we do not see the issue again, we will close it.
